title: Checksum addresses (EIP-55): why letter case matters
seoTitle: Checksum Addresses (EIP-55): Why Letter Case Matters | CRYPY
description: Why Ethereum addresses mix upper- and lower-case letters, how the EIP-55 checksum catches typos, and what it can't protect you from.
summary: How mixed upper and lower case letters catch typos in addresses.
inShort: Mixed upper and lower case in an address is a built-in typo check (EIP-55).
A mistyped checksummed address almost always fails the check.
It can't catch a look-alike address a scammer created: that one is valid.

blocks.text: An Ethereum-style address is 40 hexadecimal characters after 0x. Letters a to f can be written in upper or lower case, and the blockchain treats both the same. EIP-55 uses that freedom: the pattern of capitals is calculated from a hash of the address itself.
If one character is changed by mistake, the expected pattern no longer matches, and wallets can warn you before you send.

sections.heading: All lower case, all upper case, mixed

items: **Mixed case:** a checksummed address. Wallets can check it.
**All lower case or all upper case:** valid, but carries no check. A typo can't be caught.

blocks.text: The same address is used on every EVM chain: Ethereum, BNB Chain, Base, Arbitrum and Polygon share the same format.

sections.heading: What it can't protect you from

blocks.text: A checksum only catches accidental typos. A look-alike address that a scammer generated is a real, valid address with its own correct checksum. See [Address poisoning](guide:address-poisoning).
Never "fix" an address that fails the checksum by changing its letters until it passes. Get the correct address again from its source.

The [Address Formatter](tool:address-formatter) checks whether an address is written correctly and gives its checksummed form, for one address or a list of up to 500. It runs in your browser; nothing is sent.

faq.a: No. It is valid, it just has no typo check built in.

faq.q: My wallet says the checksum is invalid. What should I do?
faq.a: Don't send. Copy the address again from the original source; it most likely contains a typo.

faq.q: Does Bitcoin use the same checksum?
faq.a: No. EIP-55 is for Ethereum-style addresses. Other blockchains have their own address formats and checks.
